page: Microsoft Azure D96pds_v7 is a high-density, general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpdsv7 series, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is built around the 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64), delivering 96 dedicated virtual processor cores without simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 384 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core.

Storage capability is a primary highlight of the D96pds_v7, featuring an integrated 5,669 GB local NVMe solid-state drive. In addition to bundled high-capacity local scratch storage, the instance supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent managed disks. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units, focusing all compute capacity entirely on host-based ARM execution.

The ARM64 instruction set provides strong compute density and qualitative operational cost efficiency for large multi-threaded environments, though workloads must be compatible with ARM architecture and lack x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX-512. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured virtual network routing for external connectivity.

Microsoft Azure D96pds_v7 is suited for large-scale enterprise applications requiring significant parallel compute and large low-latency local storage. Target deployments include relational and distributed databases, big data analytics engines, heavy web application serving tiers, continuous integration pipelines, and local caching servers.
description: Microsoft Azure D96pds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine within the Dpdsv7 series, powered by a 64-bit ARM architecture on Microsoft Hyper-V. Designed for massive thread concurrency and balanced resource allocation, the instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs and 384 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. A key component of the hardware configuration is the integrated 5,669 GB local NVMe solid-state drive, which delivers substantial low-latency scratch and caching capacity alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and omits default public IPv4 addressing. With efficient ARM core density, the D96pds_v7 delivers an advantageous balance of compute capacity and high-throughput local I/O. It is well-matched for data-intensive enterprise workloads, including large relational and NoSQL databases, scalable web serving fleets, distributed analytics, and memory-backed batch processing pipelines.
